categories.main_business_segments: Cirrus Logic operates as a single reportable segment but reports revenue in two primary product lines: Audio Products and High-Performance Mixed-Signal (HPMS) Products. Audio Products include amplifiers, codecs, smart codecs, analog-to-digital converters, digital-to-analog converters, and standalone digital signal processors. HPMS Products encompass camera controllers, haptic and sensing solutions, and battery and power ICs, serving both traditional audio markets and expanding into broader mixed-signal applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, leveraging expertise in analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion, digital signal processing, and system-level IC engineering. As a fabless semiconductor company, Cirrus Logic outsources wafer fabrication to foundries such as TSMC and GlobalFoundries, and contracts third parties for assembly and testing, focusing its internal resources on design, R&D, and systems integration.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cirrus Logic's key customers are leading global electronics manufacturers, with Apple Inc. representing approximately 87% of total sales in fiscal 2024. The company’s products are primarily used in smartphones, laptops, tablets, AR/VR headsets, wearables, home theater systems, automotive entertainment, and professional audio systems, targeting both established and emerging consumer electronics markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with major offices and design centers in the United States (Austin, Texas), United Kingdom (Edinburgh, Scotland), China, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, and Taiwan. In fiscal 2024, 99% of net sales were international, with significant revenue generated from China, Hong Kong, India, South Korea, and Vietnam.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cirrus Logic is positioned as a fabless, downstream supplier in the semiconductor supply chain, focusing on IC design and development while relying on third-party foundries for wafer fabrication and external vendors for assembly and testing. The company manages its supply chain relationships and maintains agreements to secure wafer capacity and pricing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Cirrus Logic aims to maintain leadership in smartphone audio, increase HPMS content in smartphones, and expand into new applications and markets leveraging its mixed-signal expertise. R&D efforts are concentrated on developing new products for principal markets, advancing process technologies (e.g., 22nm nodes), and supporting customer integration from concept through production. The company also invests in emerging technologies and process transitions to drive future growth.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of proprietary semiconductor components to OEMs, contract manufacturers, and distributors. The company’s revenue is recognized upon delivery of goods, with most sales made via short-term purchase orders rather than long-term contracts, and pricing includes both fixed and variable elements such as rights of return and price protection.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Cirrus Logic faces intense competition from semiconductor suppliers such as AKM Semiconductor, Analog Devices, Realtek, Renesas, Awinic, Goodix, Skyworks, ST Microelectronics, Synaptics, and Texas Instruments. The company is a leading supplier in audio and mixed-signal processing, competing on time-to-market, product performance, integration, and customer support, but is challenged by larger competitors with broader portfolios and in-house manufacturing.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2024, Cirrus Logic reported net sales of $1.79 billion, a 5.7% decrease from $1.90 billion in 2023, with net income of $274.6 million and a gross margin of 51.2%. The company has experienced both growth and contraction in recent years, with HPMS sales showing prior growth but declining slightly in 2024. Cirrus Logic maintains strong cash flow, significant R&D investment, and a robust balance sheet, but is highly dependent on a concentrated customer base.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cirrus Logic differentiates itself through its expertise in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, enabling innovative user experiences in mobile and consumer devices. The company emphasizes custom and highly integrated solutions, strong engineering partnerships with customers, and proprietary technologies (including software algorithms and IP) that deliver superior audio quality, system integration, and power efficiency.
